result.summary: R-1 concerns: S1 supplies parsing, validation, numbered errors and its contract; S2 supplies ordered selection, array validation and its contract. No lint, type or build is configured. Match contract: src/text.js:1-7 uses strict mode, CommonJS exports, a concise public contract and TypeError; test/text.test.js:1-5 uses node:test, node:assert and named tests. New functions are public exports in local Node namespace, src/records.js is absent, and importing the module proves resolution; no persistence or migration. Assumption: split field at its first equals so remaining equals belong to the value; keys are validated as written. Exact source-check fixture comes from R-1. S1 diagnostics identify source line without echoing input; S2 throws TypeError for non-arrays. Baseline supplies runner; S1 supplies module to S2, both proofs run independently of future tests; test stage supplies durable focused cases for later regression. No other consumers or unresolved prerequisites found. Planning reference: docs/shiploop/w1-plan-reference.md; the focused suite must execute all four named cases, and the test stage owns authoring and revalidation. Backchain structural checker expects a different graph schema; its schema refusal is recorded in evidence_refs. result.summary: Retain AD-1's unit layer for src/records.js using node:test and node:assert/strict, refining the synthetic strategy with the step plan and existing package.json/test/text.test.js. Test stage creates test/records.test.js, registers four named cases TC-1 through TC-4; focused command node --test --test-reporter=spec --test-name-pattern='TC-1|TC-2|TC-3|TC-4' test/records.test.js runs at least four cases, and npm test runs the complete regression suite including those cases (smoke membership: all four). Each test starts with fresh local literals, calls the public CommonJS exports directly, is stateless with no teardown or mocks, and is due at test stage. Test and suite must be revalidated after authoring. C3 and C6 are searched, not test cases: run the step plan's exact two rg -F -n docstring searches; their unit layer is src/records.js. The field-split-at-first-equals interpretation is the accepted plan assumption; test it along with keys such as constructor. The base has no records module, so the exported functions and their behavior are absent; distinguish inability to import on base from an assertion demonstrating behavior after exports exist. The test stage should capture this limitation in RED evidence rather than claim a behavioral assertion ran on the absent module.
